knowledge_statements.statement_title: Span, Lineality, and Relative Interior of Product Cones
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Factorwise intrinsic geometry of finite Cartesian products of finite-dimensional cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty convex cones \(C_i\subseteq X_i\) in finite-dimensional spaces and \(C=\prod_{i=1}^mC_i\), \[\operatorname{span}C=\prod_{i=1}^m\operatorname{span}C_i,\qquad \operatorname{lin}C=\prod_{i=1}^m\operatorname{lin}C_i,\qquad \operatorname{ri}C=\prod_{i=1}^m\operatorname{ri}C_i.\] Hence \(C\) is full-dimensional exactly when every \(C_i\) is full-dimensional in \(X_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Span, lineality, relative interior, and full dimensionality of a finite product cone are determined componentwise.
assumptions_latex: Each \(C_i\subseteq X_i\) is a nonempty convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The span, lineality space, and relative interior of \(C\) are the products of the corresponding factor sets.
knowledge_statements.title: Span, Lineality, and Relative Interior of Product Cones
Factorwise Structure of Direct-Sum Cones
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Span, lineality, relative interior, pointedness, and solidity of a direct-sum cone are determined factorwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V=U\oplus W\) be finite-dimensional, let \(K_U\subseteq U\) and \(K_W\subseteq W\) be convex cones, and set \(K=K_U\oplus K_W\). Then \[\operatorname{span}K=\operatorname{span}K_U\oplus\operatorname{span}K_W,\quad \operatorname{lin}K=\operatorname{lin}K_U\oplus\operatorname{lin}K_W,\] and \[\operatorname{ri}K=\operatorname{ri}K_U\oplus\operatorname{ri}K_W.\] Consequently, \(K\) is pointed exactly when both factors are pointed, and \(K\) has nonempty interior in \(V\) exactly when both factors have nonempty interior in their respective complementary subspaces.
assumptions_latex: \(K_U\subseteq U\) and \(K_W\subseteq W\) are convex cones.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural invariants transported through the canonical product-to-sum isomorphism.

knowledge_statements.title: Direct-Sum Cones
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A direct-sum cone consists of sums of elements from cones in complementary subspaces. Its factor representation is unique, and in finite dimensions closed factors give a closed cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The direct-sum cone of \(K_U\) and \(K_W\) is
\[
K_U\oplus K_W:=\{u+w:u\in K_U,\ w\in K_W\}.
\]
It is a convex cone in \(V\). Because \(U\cap W=\{0\}\), each \(x\in K_U\oplus K_W\) admits a unique representation \(x=u+w\) with \(u\in K_U\) and \(w\in K_W\). If \(V\) is finite-dimensional with its standard topology and both factor cones are closed, then \(K_U\oplus K_W\) is closed in \(V\).
assumptions_latex: \(U,W\subseteq V\) are complementary linear subspaces, so \(V=U\oplus W\).
\(K_U\subseteq U\) and \(K_W\subseteq W\) are convex cones.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_U\oplus K_W\) is a convex cone, every element has a unique factorization across \(U\) and \(W\), and finite-dimensional closed factors yield a closed direct-sum cone.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic direct sums of two convex cones in complementary subspaces; the closedness assertion uses the standard finite-dimensional topology.

notation.meaning: Direct-sum cone formed from the two factor cones.
Unique components of a vector in the complementary subspaces.

source_witnesses.locator: 6.1 Convex Cones p. 111
2.3 Linear Operators and Functionals p. 31

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional intrinsic geometry across fixed complementary subspaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V=U\oplus W\) be finite-dimensional and \(K=K_U\oplus K_W\), where \(K_U\subseteq U\) and \(K_W\subseteq W\) are nonempty convex cones. Then \[\operatorname{lin}K=\operatorname{lin}K_U\oplus\operatorname{lin}K_W,\quad \operatorname{span}K=\operatorname{span}K_U\oplus\operatorname{span}K_W,\quad \operatorname{ri}K=\operatorname{ri}K_U\oplus\operatorname{ri}K_W.\] Moreover, \(K\) is pointed exactly when both factors are pointed, and \(\operatorname{int}_V K
e\varnothing\) exactly when \(\operatorname{int}_U K_U
e\varnothing\) and \(\operatorname{int}_W K_W
e\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lineality, span, relative interior, pointedness, and full dimensionality of a finite-dimensional direct-sum cone are determined factorwise.
assumptions_latex: \(K_U\subseteq U\) and \(K_W\subseteq W\) are nonempty convex cones.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Lineality, span, relative interior, pointedness, and nonempty ambient interior factor across the direct sum.
knowledge_statements.title: Factorwise Geometry of Direct-Sum Cones
Complementary-Factor Decompositions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cone decomposes across complementary subspaces exactly when both coordinate projections map it into itself; then its two cone components are unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The following conditions are equivalent:
\[
C=(C\cap U)\oplus(C\cap W),
\]
and
\[
P_U(C)\subseteq C\quad\text{and}\quad P_W(C)\subseteq C.
\]
Under either condition, every \(x\in C\) has the unique decomposition \(x=P_Ux+P_Wx\), where \(P_Ux\in C\cap U\) and \(P_Wx\in C\cap W\). Thus the coordinate map \(x\mapsto(P_Ux,P_Wx)\) identifies \(C\) with the product cone \((C\cap U)\times(C\cap W)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C=(C\cap U)\oplus(C\cap W)\) exactly when both coordinate projections preserve \(C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterization of when a cone separates exactly across fixed complementary factors.

notation.meaning: Coordinate projections associated with the complementary decomposition.
Cone factors lying in the complementary subspaces.

children.title: Minkowski Sums of Cones
children.top_down_role: Additive combination of conic direction systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Algebraic Laws for Cone Sums
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cone addition is commutative, associative, monotone, unital, and idempotent; the sum is the smallest cone containing both summands.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For convex cones \(K,L,M\subseteq V\), \[K+L=L+K,\qquad (K+L)+M=K+(L+M),\qquad K+\{0\}=K,\qquad K+K=K.\] Addition is monotone in each argument, and \(K+L\) is the smallest convex cone containing both \(K\) and \(L\). Equivalently, \[K+L=\operatorname{cone}(K\cup L).\]
assumptions_latex: \(K,L,M\) are convex cones in a common real vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K+L=\operatorname{cone}(K\cup L),\text{ with cone addition commutative, associative, monotone, and idempotent}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Purely algebraic identities for convex cones in a common vector space.

knowledge_statements.title: Minkowski Sums of Cones
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Minkowski sum contains every sum of one element from each cone. It is a convex cone, but even in finite dimensions it need not be closed when both summands are closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Minkowski sum of \(K_1\) and \(K_2\) is
\[
K_1+K_2:=\{x_1+x_2:x_1\in K_1,\ x_2\in K_2\}.
\]
It is a convex cone. Even when \(K_1\) and \(K_2\) are closed, \(K_1+K_2\) need not be closed.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space with its standard topology.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_1+K_2\) is the convex cone consisting of all pairwise sums from the two cones, and closedness of the summands does not ensure closedness of the sum.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite Minkowski addition of convex cones in one finite-dimensional ambient vector space.

source_witnesses.locator: 3 Convex Sets p. 49
6.1 Convex Cones p. 111

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-image representation separating algebraic preservation from topological closedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For convex cones \(K_1,K_2\subseteq V\), let \(A:V\times V\to V\) be \(A(x_1,x_2)=x_1+x_2\). Then \[K_1+K_2=A(K_1\times K_2).\] Thus the sum is a linear image of a product cone; convexity and conicity are preserved, but closedness need not be.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cone sum is the image of the product cone under coordinate addition, which preserves convex conicity but not necessarily closedness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_1+K_2=A(K_1\times K_2)\), without a general closedness guarantee.
knowledge_statements.title: Cone Sums as Addition-Map Images

children.title: Generated Joins of Cones
children.top_down_role: Smallest conic containers generated by multiple cone families.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual of a Generated Cone Join
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The positive dual of a join generated by any family of cones is the intersection of the factor duals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((K_i)_{i\in I}\) be convex cones in a real inner-product space and let \(K=\bigvee_{i\in I}K_i\). Then \[K^*=\bigcap_{i\in I}K_i^*.\] Thus a vector is nonnegative on the generated join exactly when it is nonnegative on every generating cone.
assumptions_latex: \((K_i)_{i\in I}\) is a nonempty family of convex cones in a real inner-product space.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-dual convention; valid for arbitrary nonempty families without closedness assumptions.

notation.meaning: Generated join of the cone family.

knowledge_statements.title: Generated Joins of Cones
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The join of cone families is their smallest common convex cone, formed by all finite sums of elements selected from the constituent cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The generated join of the family is
\[
\bigvee_{i\in I}K_i
=\operatorname{cone}\!\left(\bigcup_{i\in I}K_i\right)
=\left\{\sum_{j=1}^{m}x_j:m\in\mathbb N,\ x_j\in K_{i_j},\ i_j\in I\right\}.
\]
It is the unique smallest convex cone containing every \(K_i\): if \(D\) is a convex cone and \(K_i\subseteq D\) for all \(i\in I\), then \(\bigvee_{i\in I}K_i\subseteq D\). For finite \(I\), the join equals the iterated Minkowski sum.
assumptions_latex: \((K_i)_{i\in I}\) is a nonempty family of convex cones in \(V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The join is the conic hull of the union, equivalently the set of finite sums drawn from the family.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Join in the inclusion-ordered family of convex cones.

notation.meaning: Smallest convex cone containing every member of the family.

source_witnesses.locator: 6.1 Convex Cones p. 111

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-reversing duality for an arbitrary nonempty family of convex cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty family of convex cones \((K_i)_{i\in I}\) in a finite-dimensional inner-product space, \[\left(\bigvee_{i\in I}K_i\right)^*=\bigcap_{i\in I}K_i^*=\left(\overline{\bigvee_{i\in I}K_i}\right)^*.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duality converts an arbitrarily generated cone join into the intersection of the factor dual cones, and closing the join does not change its dual.
assumptions_latex: \((K_i)_{i\in I}\) is a nonempty family of convex cones in a finite-dimensional inner-product space.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual of a Generated Join

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Joins in the Lattice of Closed Convex Cones
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes algebraic joins from joins within the class of closed convex cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty family of closed convex cones \((K_i)_{i\in I}\) in a finite-dimensional vector space, their meet among closed convex cones is \(\bigcap_{i\in I}K_i\), while their join is \[\overline{\operatorname{cone}\!\left(\bigcup_{i\in I}K_i\right)}.\] The closure cannot generally be omitted, even for two closed convex cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closed convex cones form a lattice whose join is the closure of the algebraically generated join; the closure can be essential.
assumptions_latex: \((K_i)_{i\in I}\) is a nonempty family of closed convex cones.
The ambient vector space is finite-dimensional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The closed-cone meet is \(\bigcap_iK_i\), and the closed-cone join is \(\overline{\operatorname{cone}(\bigcup_iK_i)}\).

notation.meaning: Join within the class of closed convex cones

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Join Generated by a Family of Convex Cones
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(E\) is a real vector space and \((K_i)_{i\in I}\) is a nonempty family of convex cones contained in \(E\). If closure is used, \(E\) also carries a fixed vector topology.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The algebraic join is the least convex cone containing every family member; the closed join is the least closed convex cone containing them.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The generated join of \((K_i)_{i\in I}\) is \[\bigvee_{i\in I}K_i:=\bigcap\{K\subseteq E:K\text{ is a convex cone and }K_i\subseteq K\ \forall i\}.\] Equivalently, \[\bigvee_{i\in I}K_i=\operatorname{cone}\!\left(\bigcup_{i\in I}K_i\right)=\left\{\sum_{j=1}^m x_j:m\ge1,\ x_j\in K_{i_j},\ i_j\in I\right\}.\] Its closed join is \[\overline{\bigvee}_{i\in I}K_i:=\overline{\operatorname{cone}}\!\left(\bigcup_{i\in I}K_i\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The join of a family of cones is the smallest convex cone containing every member of the family. It consists of finite sums of elements selected from the component cones. Taking closure gives the smallest closed convex cone containing the family.
assumptions_latex: Each \(K_i\subseteq E\) is a convex cone.
A topology on \(E\) is fixed for the closed join.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(\forall i)\ K_i\subseteq\bigvee_iK_i,\qquad \bigvee_iK_i\subseteq L\] for every convex cone \(L\) satisfying \((\forall i)\ K_i\subseteq L\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a finite family, \(\bigvee_{i=1}^mK_i=K_1+\cdots+K_m\).
The join equals the conic hull of the union of the component cones.
special_cases_latex: If the family is nested and has a largest member \(K_j\), then \(\bigvee_iK_i=K_j\).
For rays \(K_i=\mathbb R_+u_i\), the join is the cone generated by the vectors \(u_i\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The join operation is commutative, associative, and idempotent at the level of cone families.
The polar of a finite join is the intersection of the component polar cones.
The algebraic join need not be closed, so the closed join can be strictly larger.
boundary_notes: Only finite sums occur in the algebraic join, even when the index set is infinite.
Topological infinite sums are not included unless a separate convergence convention is specified.

notation.meaning: least closed convex cone containing all \(K_i\)

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) be a real topological vector space, let \(K\subseteq X\) be a cone, and let \(S\subseteq X\) be another cone, a linear subspace, or an affine subspace.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition covers set-theoretic sections in a common ambient space. It distinguishes homogeneous sections, which remain cones, from affine sections, which generally do not contain the origin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The section of \(K\) by \(S\) is \[K|_S:=K\cap S=\{x\in X:x\in K\text{ and }x\in S\}.\] If \(S\) is a cone, then \(K|_S\) is a cone. If both \(K\) and \(S\) are convex, then \(K|_S\) is convex; if both are closed, then it is closed. For a linear subspace \(L\leq X\), the subspace section is \(K\cap L\), regarded intrinsically as a cone in \(L\). For an affine subspace \(A=x_0+L\), the affine section is \(K\cap A\); after choosing \(x_0\in K\cap A\), its translated representative is \((K\cap A)-x_0\subseteq L\), but this translation need not be a cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The section of a cone \(K\) by a set \(S\) in the same space is the intersection \(K\cap S\). A section by another cone is again a cone, and convexity or closedness is inherited when both intersected sets have the corresponding property. A section by a linear subspace is naturally treated as a cone in that subspace. An affine section \(K\cap(x_0+L)\) is generally only a convex set in the affine space and need not itself be a cone, because it need not contain the origin.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq X\) is a cone: \(x\in K,\ \lambda\geq0\Rightarrow \lambda x\in K\).
\(S\subseteq X\) is specified in the same ambient space as \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K|_S=K\cap S\), with conic structure inherited when \(S\) is a cone and intrinsic subspace geometry used when \(S=L\leq X\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(x\in K|_S\iff x\in K\ \wedge\ x\in S\).
For a linear inclusion \(i_L:L\hookrightarrow X\), \(K\cap L=i_L^{-1}(K)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(S=K_2\) is a convex cone, then \(K|_{K_2}=K\cap K_2\) is the cone of common feasible directions.
If \(S=\ker A\) for a linear map \(A:X\to Y\), then \(K|_S=\{x\in K:Ax=0\}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Arbitrary intersections of convex cone sections are convex cones.
If \(X\) is Hausdorff and \(K\) and \(S\) are closed, then \(K|_S\) is closed.
boundary_notes: An affine section not passing through \(0\) is not a cone in \(X\).
The definition does not assert that a nonempty affine section has a canonical choice of translation point.

notation.meaning: section of the cone K by S
canonical inclusion of a subspace L into X

children.title: Intersections of Cones
children.top_down_role: Common positive directions and inherited structural properties.

knowledge_statements.title: Interior Can Be Lost under Cone Intersection
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two full-dimensional closed pointed cones can intersect in a single ray, so nonempty ambient interior is not inherited.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
In \(\mathbb R^2\), let
\[
K_1=\operatorname{cone}\{(1,0),(0,1)\},\qquad
K_2=\operatorname{cone}\{(1,0),(0,-1)\}.
\]
Both cones are closed, pointed, and have nonempty ambient interior, but
\[
K_1\cap K_2=\{(t,0):t\geq0\}
\]
has empty ambient interior.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional pointed example witnessing failure of ambient-interior inheritance.

knowledge_statements.title: Lineality of a Cone Intersection
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lineality commutes with arbitrary cone intersections, giving an exact pointedness criterion that is weaker than requiring every factor to be pointed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((K_i)_{i\in I}\) be a nonempty family of convex cones in a real vector space. Then
\[
\operatorname{lin}\!\left(\bigcap_{i\in I}K_i\right)=\bigcap_{i\in I}\operatorname{lin}(K_i).
\]
Consequently, \(\bigcap_iK_i\) is pointed exactly when \(\bigcap_i\operatorname{lin}(K_i)=\{0\}\).
assumptions_latex: \((K_i)_{i\in I}\) is a nonempty family of convex cones in a real vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{lin}(\bigcap_iK_i)=\bigcap_i\operatorname{lin}(K_i)\), and the intersection is pointed iff this common lineality is \(\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact algebraic lineality and pointedness rule for arbitrary intersections of convex cones.

knowledge_statements.title: Relative Interior of a Qualified Finite Intersection
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finitely many cones with a common relative-interior point, relative interior commutes with intersection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K_1,\ldots,K_m\) be nonempty convex cones in a finite-dimensional real vector space. If
\[
\bigcap_{j=1}^m\operatorname{ri}K_j\neq\varnothing,
\]
then
\[
\operatorname{ri}\!\left(\bigcap_{j=1}^mK_j\right)=\bigcap_{j=1}^m\operatorname{ri}K_j.
\]
assumptions_latex: The ambient real vector space is finite-dimensional.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional finite-intersection rule under the common-relative-interior qualification.

notation.meaning: Relative interior in the affine hull.

knowledge_statements.title: Intersections of Cones
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any intersection of convex cones is a convex cone. Closedness and pointedness are inherited when all factors have them, but nonempty interior may be lost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The intersection
\[
K:=\bigcap_{i\in I}K_i
\]
is a convex cone. If every \(K_i\) is closed, then \(K\) is closed. If every \(K_i\) is pointed, then \(K\) is pointed. Nonempty interior is not generally inherited by arbitrary intersections.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a real topological vector space.
\((K_i)_{i\in I}\) is a nonempty family of convex cones in \(V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigcap_{i\in I}K_i\) is a convex cone; it is closed or pointed when every factor has the corresponding property, while nonempty interior need not be inherited.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arbitrary intersections and their basic convexity, closedness, pointedness, and interior behavior.

notation.meaning: Common cone of all family members.

source_witnesses.locator: 3 Convex Sets p. 49
6.1 Convex Cones p. 111

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit finite-family witness for failure of inherited nonempty ambient interior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In \(\mathbb R^2\), let \(K_+=\{(x,y):y\geq0\}\) and \(K_-=\{(x,y):y\leq0\}\). Both cones have nonempty interiors, but \(K_+\cap K_-=\mathbb R\times\{0\}\) has empty ambient interior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The upper and lower half-space cones have nonempty interiors, while their intersection is a line with empty ambient interior.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lineality and Pointedness of Cone Intersections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact lineality formula strengthening the seed's sufficient pointedness condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\bigcap_{i\in I}K_i\), \[\operatorname{lin}K=\bigcap_{i\in I}\operatorname{lin}K_i.\] Consequently, \(K\) is pointed if and only if \(\bigcap_{i\in I}\operatorname{lin}K_i=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lineality space of an intersection is the intersection of the factors' lineality spaces, giving an exact pointedness criterion.
assumptions_latex: \((K_i)_{i\in I}\) is a nonempty family of convex cones in \(V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{lin}(\bigcap_iK_i)=\bigcap_i\operatorname{lin}K_i\), and the intersection is pointed exactly when this space is \(\{0\}\).

notation.meaning: Lineality space of a convex cone.

knowledge_statements.title: Lineality and Pointedness of Cone Intersections

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite intersections; relative-interior equality requires a common relative-interior point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty finite family, \[\operatorname{int}\!\left(\bigcap_iK_i\right)=\bigcap_i\operatorname{int}K_i.\] If additionally \(V\) is finite-dimensional and \(\bigcap_i\operatorname{ri}K_i\neq\varnothing\), then \[\operatorname{ri}\!\left(\bigcap_iK_i\right)=\bigcap_i\operatorname{ri}K_i.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ambient interior distributes over finite intersections. Relative interior does so when the factors have a common relative-interior point.
assumptions_latex: \((K_i)_{i\in I}\) is a nonempty finite family of convex cones.
For the relative-interior identity, \(V\) is finite-dimensional and \(\bigcap_i\operatorname{ri}K_i\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.title: Interior and Relative-Interior Intersection Rules

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) be a real vector space, let \(I\) be an index set, and let \((K_i)_{i\in I}\) be cones contained in \(X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is an arbitrary-family definition. Empty-index intersections follow the set-theoretic convention \(\bigcap_{i\in\varnothing}K_i=X\), which is itself a cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The intersection cone of \((K_i)_{i\in I}\) is \[K_{\cap}:=\bigcap_{i\in I}K_i=\{x\in X:(\forall i\in I)\ x\in K_i\}.\] It is a cone because \(x\in K_{\cap}\) and \(\lambda\geq0\) imply \(\lambda x\in K_i\) for every \(i\), hence \(\lambda x\in K_{\cap}\). If every \(K_i\) is convex, then \(K_{\cap}\) is convex. If \(X\) is topological and every \(K_i\) is closed, then \(K_{\cap}\) is closed. Thus the operation represents the directions simultaneously admitted by every member of the family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The intersection of a family of cones \((K_i)_{i\in I}\) in a common vector space is the set of vectors belonging to every \(K_i\). This set is always a cone. It inherits convexity if all members are convex and, in a topological vector space, inherits closedness if all members are closed. The intersection therefore encodes common positive directions without adding any new direction.
assumptions_latex: \((\forall i\in I)(\forall x\in K_i)(\forall\lambda\geq0)\ \lambda x\in K_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_{\cap}=\bigcap_{i\in I}K_i\) is a cone, and it is convex or closed whenever every \(K_i\) has the corresponding property.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(x\in K_{\cap}\iff(\forall i\in I)\ x\in K_i\).
\(K_{\cap}\) is the greatest cone \(C\subseteq X\) satisfying \(C\subseteq K_i\) for every \(i\in I\).
special_cases_latex: For two cones, \(K_1\cap K_2=\{x:x\in K_1\text{ and }x\in K_2\}\).
For a cone \(K\) and subspace \(L\), \(K\cap L\) is their common conic section.
immediate_consequences_latex: If each \(K_i\) is pointed, then a nonempty intersection is pointed.
If at least one \(K_j\) is pointed, then \(K_{\cap}\subseteq K_j\) is pointed.
boundary_notes: The cones must lie in a common ambient vector space unless explicit embeddings are supplied.
An infinite intersection may have empty interior even when every member has nonempty interior.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Intersections as Meets of Convex Cones
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-theoretic characterization in the inclusion-ordered class of convex cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty family \((K_i)_{i\in I}\) of convex cones, \(K=\bigcap_{i\in I}K_i\) is their greatest lower bound under inclusion: \[K\subseteq K_i\quad(i\in I),\] and whenever a convex cone \(D\) satisfies \(D\subseteq K_i\) for every \(i\), one has \(D\subseteq K\). Thus arbitrary meets exist in the inclusion lattice of convex cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The intersection of a family of convex cones is exactly their greatest common subcone, or meet, under inclusion.

children.title: Subspace Sections
children.top_down_role: Cones restricted to linear subspaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Failure without the Relative-Interior Qualification
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The relative-interior formula can fail when the subspace does not meet the cone's relative interior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C=\mathbb R_+^2\) and \(L=\mathbb R\times\{0\}\). Then
\[
L\cap\operatorname{ri}C=\varnothing,
\qquad
\operatorname{ri}(C\cap L)=\{(t,0):t>0\},
\]
so \(\operatorname{ri}(C\cap L)\neq\operatorname{ri}C\cap L\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp planar failure of relative-interior commutation for a subspace section.

knowledge_statements.title: Lineality of a Subspace Section
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lineality of a subspace section is the intersection of the cone's lineality with the subspace, yielding an exact pointedness test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq V\) be a convex cone and \(L\subseteq V\) a linear subspace. Then
\[
\operatorname{lin}(C\cap L)=\operatorname{lin}(C)\cap L.
\]
Hence \(C\cap L\) is pointed exactly when \(L\cap\operatorname{lin}(C)=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{lin}(C\cap L)=\operatorname{lin}(C)\cap L\), and \(C\cap L\) is pointed iff \(L\cap\operatorname{lin}(C)=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact lineality identity for restricting a convex cone to a linear subspace.

knowledge_statements.title: Relative Interior of a Qualified Subspace Section
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the subspace meets the relative interior of the cone, relative interior commutes with taking the section.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V\) be finite-dimensional, let \(C\subseteq V\) be a nonempty convex cone, and let \(L\subseteq V\) be a linear subspace. If
\[
L\cap\operatorname{ri}C\neq\varnothing,
\]
then
\[
\operatorname{ri}(C\cap L)=\operatorname{ri}C\cap L.
\]
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq V\) is a nonempty convex cone.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional section rule under the essential relative-interior qualification.

notation.meaning: Relative interior in the affine hull.

knowledge_statements.title: Subspace Sections
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subspace section restricts a cone to directions lying in a linear subspace. Convexity and pointedness pass to the section, and closedness passes under the stated topological conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The section of \(C\) by \(L\) is
\[
C|_L:=C\cap L,
\]
regarded as a cone in the vector space \(L\). It is a convex cone. If \(V\) is a topological vector space, \(L\) has the relative topology, and \(C\) is closed in \(V\), then \(C|_L\) is closed in \(L\). If \(C\) is pointed, then \(C|_L\) is pointed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The subspace section \(C\cap L\) is a convex cone in \(L\), with closedness and pointedness inherited under the stated conditions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restriction of a cone to a linear subspace, with relative topology understood when topological properties are asserted.

notation.meaning: Restriction of the cone to the subspace.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual Cone of a Closed Subspace Section
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The section dual is computed in \(L\); closedness of \(C\) is essential for this unconditional formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With the positive-dual convention, \[(C\cap L)^*_{L}=\operatorname{cl}_{L}\bigl(P_L(C^*)\bigr).\] If \(P_L(C^*)\) is closed in \(L\), the closure may be omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a closed cone, the dual of its subspace section is the closure of the projection of its ambient dual.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq V\) is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Cone of a Closed Subspace Section

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes interior in the section space from ambient interior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(L\subsetneq V\), every subset of \(L\), including \(C\cap L\), has empty interior in \(V\). Nevertheless, \(C\cap L\) may have nonempty interior in \(L\); for \(C=V\), \(C\cap L=L\) and \(\operatorname{int}_L(C\cap L)=L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A section by a proper subspace has empty ambient interior even when it is full-dimensional within the subspace.
assumptions_latex: \(L\subsetneq V\) is a proper linear subspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{int}_V(C\cap L)=\varnothing\), while \(\operatorname{int}_L(C\cap L)\) can be nonempty.
knowledge_statements.title: Section Topology Must Be Relative

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lineality and Pointedness of a Subspace Section
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact section-specific pointedness criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(D=C\cap L\), \[\operatorname{lin}D=\operatorname{lin}C\cap L.\] Hence \(D\), regarded as a cone in \(L\), is pointed if and only if \(\operatorname{lin}C\cap L=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A section's lineality is the part of the cone's lineality lying in the subspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{lin}(C\cap L)=\operatorname{lin}C\cap L\), with pointedness equivalent to this space being \(\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Lineality and Pointedness of a Subspace Section

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finiteness is modulo multiplication by nonzero real scalars.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(N\in\mathbb N\) and every linear subspace \(L\subseteq\mathbb R^N\), the elementary vectors of \(L\) form only finitely many equivalence classes under \(z\sim z'\iff z'=\lambda z\) for some \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}\).

children.title: Linear Cone Transport Calculus
children.top_down_role: Transport of cones through linear transformations and quotient constructions.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be real vector spaces, let \(A:X\to Y\) be linear, let \(K\subseteq X\) be a cone, and let \(Q\subseteq Y\) be a cone.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition is algebraic. Closedness requires separate topological hypotheses and is not automatically transported by a linear image.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Linear cone transport comprises the forward image and inverse image operations \[A(K):=\{Ax:x\in K\}\subseteq Y,\qquad A^{-1}(Q):=\{x\in X:Ax\in Q\}\subseteq X.\] Both sets are cones. If \(K\) and \(Q\) are convex, then \(A(K)\) and \(A^{-1}(Q)\) are convex. When \(A\) is surjective, the quotient cone induced by \(K\) on \(X/\ker A\) is \(\pi(K)\), where \(\pi:X\to X/\ker A\) is the quotient map; the induced isomorphism \(\widetilde A:X/\ker A\to Y\) satisfies \(A(K)=\widetilde A(\pi(K))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cone is transported forward through a linear map by taking all images \(Ax\) of its elements, and transported backward by taking all points whose images lie in a target cone. Both operations preserve conic and convex structure. For a surjective map, forward transport factors through the quotient by the kernel: first project the cone to \(X/\ker A\), then apply the induced linear isomorphism. Closedness is not part of the purely algebraic transport rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A(K)\) and \(A^{-1}(Q)\) are cones; for surjective \(A\), \(A(K)=\widetilde A(\pi(K))\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(y\in A(K)\iff(\exists x\in K)\ y=Ax\).
\(x\in A^{-1}(Q)\iff Ax\in Q\).
special_cases_latex: If \(A\) is injective, then \(A:K\to A(K)\) is a conic isomorphism onto its image.
boundary_notes: A continuous linear image of a closed convex cone need not be closed.
For nonlinear maps, neither image nor inverse image is governed by this linear transport definition.

notation.meaning: linear image of K under A
inverse image of Q under A
quotient map onto X modulo the kernel of A

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear Images and Coordinate Projections of Cones
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X,Y\) be finite-dimensional real vector spaces, let \(K\subseteq X\) be a cone, and let \(A:X\to Y\) be linear. For a decomposition \(X=U\oplus V\), let \(P_U:X\to U\) be the canonical projection.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The record treats forward images, including coordinate projections, in finite dimensions. It does not impose a closed-image hypothesis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The linear image cone is \[A K:=\{Ax:x\in K\}.\] Under a decomposition \(X=U\oplus V\), the projected cone is \[P_UK=\{u\in U:(\exists v\in V)\ u+v\in K\}.\] These are cones, and they are convex whenever \(K\) is convex. The fibers of the image are \(K\cap A^{-1}(y)\), so membership in \(AK\) is equivalent to nonemptiness of the corresponding fiber. Although continuity gives \(A(\operatorname{cl}K)\subseteq\operatorname{cl}(AK)\), equality and closedness of \(AK\) require additional conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The image of a cone \(K\) under a linear map \(A\) is the set of all vectors \(Ax\) with \(x\in K\). A coordinate projection is the special case in which \(A=P_U\); a vector \(u\) belongs to the projection exactly when some eliminated component \(v\) makes \(u+v\) belong to \(K\). Images and projections preserve conic and convex structure but do not generally preserve closedness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(AK\) is a cone, and \(P_UK=\{u\in U:(\exists v\in V)\ u+v\in K\}\) for \(X=U\oplus V\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(y\in AK\iff K\cap A^{-1}(y)\neq\varnothing\).
\(AK\) is the projection onto \(Y\) of \(\{(x,y)\in K\times Y:y=Ax\}\).
special_cases_latex: If \(A\) is invertible, \(AK\) is linearly isomorphic to \(K\).
If \(K\) is polyhedral, then \(AK\) is polyhedral and hence closed in finite dimensions.
immediate_consequences_latex: \(A(\operatorname{ri}K)=\operatorname{ri}(AK)\) for nonempty convex \(K\) in finite dimensions.
If \(K\) is compact, then \(AK\) is compact and therefore closed.
boundary_notes: A closed unbounded convex cone can have a nonclosed projection.
Projection here means a linear coordinate projection, not metric projection onto a cone.

notation.meaning: projection associated with X=U direct-sum V

knowledge_statements.title: Relative Interior Commutes with Linear Images
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In finite dimensions, the relative interior of a nonempty convex cone maps exactly onto the relative interior of its linear image.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V,W\) be finite-dimensional real vector spaces, let \(A:V\to W\) be linear, and let \(C\subseteq V\) be a nonempty convex cone. Then
\[
A(\operatorname{ri}C)=\operatorname{ri}(A(C)).
\]
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq V\) is a nonempty convex cone.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional image theorem for nonempty convex cones; no closedness assumption is required.

notation.meaning: Relative interior in the affine hull.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Images of Cones
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear map sends a convex cone to a convex cone. Injectivity preserves pointedness, while closedness requires additional regularity and can otherwise fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The linear image
\[
A(C):=\{Ax:x\in C\}
\]
is a convex cone in \(W\). If \(A\) is injective and \(C\) is pointed, then \(A(C)\) is pointed. If \(V\) and \(W\) are finite-dimensional, \(C\) is closed, and \(C\cap\ker A=\{0\}\), then \(A(C)\) is closed. Without an additional regularity condition, the image of a closed convex cone can be nonclosed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A(C)\) is a convex cone in \(W\), though closedness may fail.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic cone preservation under arbitrary linear mappings.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Pointedness Criterion for a Cone Image
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Kernel-face characterization, strengthening the seed's injectivity-based sufficient condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The image cone \(A(C)\) is pointed if and only if \(C\cap\ker A\) is a face of \(C\). In particular, injectivity of \(A\) preserves pointedness of a pointed cone because then \(C\cap\ker A=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cone image is pointed exactly when the part of the cone collapsed to zero is a face of the original cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A(C)\text{ is pointed}\iff C\cap\ker A\text{ is a face of }C\).
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Pointedness Criterion for a Cone Image

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Span and Functoriality of Cone Images
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic structural identities for forward cone transport.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For linear maps \(A:V\to W\) and \(B:W\to Z\), \[\operatorname{span}A(C)=A(\operatorname{span}C),\qquad B(A(C))=(B\circ A)(C).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The span of an image cone is the image of the original span, and forward cone images compose with linear maps.
knowledge_statements.title: Span and Functoriality of Cone Images

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generators and Polyhedrality Under Linear Images
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-generator transport; general closedness failures remain in the sibling boundary leaf.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(C=\operatorname{cone}\{v_1,\ldots,v_m\}\), then \[A(C)=\operatorname{cone}\{Av_1,\ldots,Av_m\}.\] Thus linear images preserve finite generation; in finite dimensions they preserve polyhedrality and hence closedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear map transports a finite generating family by mapping each generator, preserving finite generation and finite-dimensional polyhedrality.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is generated by finitely many vectors.
For the polyhedral conclusion, the spaces are finite-dimensional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A(\operatorname{cone}\{v_i\})=\operatorname{cone}\{Av_i\}\), so finite generation and finite-dimensional polyhedrality pass to the image.
knowledge_statements.title: Generators and Polyhedrality Under Linear Images
Dual Cone of an Orthogonal Projection
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual within the projection subspace of an orthogonally projected cone is the section of the original dual cone by that subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, let \(L\subseteq V\) be a linear subspace, and let \(C\subseteq V\) be a convex cone. Then
\[
(P_LC)^*_L=C^*\cap L,
\]
where the left dual is formed in the inner-product space \(L\).
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space.
\(L\subseteq V\) is a linear subspace with orthogonal projector \(P_L\).
Dual cones use the nonnegative-pairing convention.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Duality is taken inside the projection subspace under the nonnegative convention.

notation.meaning: Dual of the projected cone in the inner-product space \(L\).

knowledge_statements.title: Cone Projections
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projecting a cone onto a subspace yields a convex cone equal to the section of its orthogonal-complement enlargement; the projected cone may be nonclosed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The projected cone is
\[
P_L(C):=\{P_Lx:x\in C\}\subseteq L.
\]
It is a convex cone and has the representation
\[
P_L(C)=(C+L^\perp)\cap L.
\]
Consequently, \(P_L(C)\) is closed exactly when \((C+L^\perp)\cap L\) is closed in \(L\). Closedness of \(C\) alone does not guarantee closedness of \(P_L(C)\).
assumptions_latex: \(L\subseteq V\) is a linear subspace with orthogonal projector \(P_L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_L(C)\) is a convex cone in \(L\), and \(P_L(C)=(C+L^\perp)\cap L\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthogonal coordinate projection, not nearest-point projection onto the cone itself.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual and Closed Hull of a Projected Cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthogonal coordinate projection; duals are computed in the target subspace using the positive-pairing convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(D=P_L(C)\subseteq L\), \[D^*_{L}=C^*\cap L.\] Consequently, \[\operatorname{cl}_{L}P_L(C)=(C^*\cap L)^*_{L}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual of a projected cone is the section of the original dual by the target subspace; dualizing again gives the projected cone's closed hull.

notation.meaning: Positive dual of \(D\subseteq L\), computed in \(L\).

knowledge_statements.title: Dual and Closed Hull of a Projected Cone
Image Closedness Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projecting the positive-semidefinite two-by-two cone onto two matrix entries gives a nonclosed cone containing a sequence that approaches a missing boundary point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The image of the closed convex cone \(C\) is
\[
A(C)=\{(a,b)\in\mathbb R^2:a>0\}\cup\{(0,0)\}.
\]
This image is not closed: \((1/n,1)\in A(C)\) for every integer \(n\geq1\), the sequence converges to \((0,1)\), and \((0,1)\notin A(C)\). Thus a linear image, including a coordinate projection, need not preserve closedness of a closed convex cone.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb S^2\) is the space of real symmetric \(2\times2\) matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The closed cone \(C\) has the nonclosed linear image \(A(C)=\{(a,b)\in\mathbb R^2:a>0\}\cup\{(0,0)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete finite-dimensional boundary showing that closed cones can have nonclosed linear images.

notation.meaning: Linear map retaining the first diagonal and off-diagonal entries.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Missing Image Points and Strict Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes points outside the image closure from weakly infeasible missing boundary points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With \(C^*=\{s:\langle s,x\rangle\geq0\ \forall x\in C\}\), \[b\in\operatorname{cl}A(C)\iff \langle y,b\rangle\geq0\quad\text{for every }y\text{ with }A^*y\in C^*.\] Hence \(b\notin\operatorname{cl}A(C)\) admits \(y\) with \(A^*y\in C^*\) and \(\langle y,b\rangle<0\), whereas \(b\in\operatorname{cl}A(C)\setminus A(C)\) is infeasible without such a strict separator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Points outside the closed image have strict adjoint-dual certificates, while missing boundary points are infeasible but cannot be strictly separated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A strict adjoint-dual separator exists exactly when \(b\notin\operatorname{cl}A(C)\), not when \(b\in\operatorname{cl}A(C)\setminus A(C)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Missing Image Points and Strict Separation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-dimensional characterization of image closedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every cone \(C\subseteq V\), \[A^{-1}(A(C))=C+\ker A.\] If \(V,W\) are finite-dimensional, then \[A(C)\text{ is closed in }W\iff C+\ker A\text{ is closed in }V.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cone image is closed exactly when its kernel-saturated preimage is closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A(C)\) is closed if and only if \(C+\ker A\) is closed.
knowledge_statements.title: Closedness via Kernel Saturation

children.title: Inverse Images of Cones
children.top_down_role: Pullback of conic structure through linear mappings.

knowledge_statements.title: Failure of Pullback Relative-Interior Calculus without Qualification
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the map's range misses the relative interior of the target cone, relative interior need not commute with pullback.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^2\) be \(A(t)=(t,0)\) and let \(K=\mathbb R_+^2\). Then
\[
\operatorname{ran}A\cap\operatorname{ri}K=\varnothing,
\qquad A^{-1}K=\mathbb R_+,
\]
so
\[
\operatorname{ri}(A^{-1}K)=(0,\infty)
eq A^{-1}(\operatorname{ri}K)=\varnothing.
\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp planar range-qualification failure for a cone pullback.

knowledge_statements.title: Lineality of an Inverse-Image Cone
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lineality pulls back exactly. The pullback is pointed precisely when the map is injective and its range meets the target lineality only at zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A:V\to W\) be linear and let \(K\subseteq W\) be a convex cone. Then
\[
\operatorname{lin}(A^{-1}K)=A^{-1}(\operatorname{lin}K).
\]
Consequently, \(A^{-1}K\) is pointed if and only if
\[
\ker A=\{0\}\quad\text{and}\quad\operatorname{ran}A\cap\operatorname{lin}K=\{0\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact algebraic lineality and pointedness rule for a cone pullback.

knowledge_statements.title: Relative Interior of a Qualified Cone Pullback
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the range of the map meets the relative interior of the target cone, relative interior commutes with pullback.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V,W\) be finite-dimensional real vector spaces, let \(A:V\to W\) be linear, and let \(K\subseteq W\) be a nonempty convex cone. If
\[
\operatorname{ran}A\cap\operatorname{ri}K\neq\varnothing,
\]
then
\[
\operatorname{ri}(A^{-1}K)=A^{-1}(\operatorname{ri}K).
\]
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq W\) is a nonempty convex cone.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional pullback rule under the standard range qualification.

notation.meaning: Relative interior in the affine hull.

knowledge_statements.title: Inverse Images of Cones
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The pullback consists of vectors mapped into the cone. It is a convex cone containing the kernel, continuity preserves closedness under pullback, and pullback commutes with arbitrary intersections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The inverse-image cone is
\[
A^{-1}(K):=\{x\in V:Ax\in K\}.
\]
It is a convex cone in \(V\), and \(\ker A\subseteq A^{-1}(K)\). If \(V\) and \(W\) are topological vector spaces, \(A\) is continuous, and \(K\) is closed, then \(A^{-1}(K)\) is closed. Inverse images also commute with arbitrary intersections:
\[
A^{-1}\!\left(\bigcap_{i\in I}K_i\right)=\bigcap_{i\in I}A^{-1}(K_i).
\]
assumptions_latex: \((K_i)_{i\in I}\) is a family of convex cones in \(W\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A^{-1}(K)\) is a convex cone containing \(\ker A\); closedness is preserved by continuous \(A\), and inverse images commute with arbitrary intersections.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pullback of convex cones through linear maps, including preservation of intersections.

notation.meaning: Inverse image of the cone under the linear map.

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3 Linear Operators and Functionals p. 31
6.1 Convex Cones p. 111

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual Cone of a Closed Linear Pullback
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-dimensional dual formula; closedness of the target cone prevents loss of information before intersection with the map range.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With the positive-dual convention, \[(A^{-1}K)^*=\operatorname{cl}\bigl(A^*(K^*)\bigr).\] If \(A^*(K^*)\) is closed, the closure may be omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a closed target cone, the dual of its pullback is the closure of the adjoint image of the target dual.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq W\) is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Cone of a Closed Linear Pullback

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lineality and Pointedness of Pullback Cones
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact lineality formula and pointedness characterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(D=A^{-1}(K)\), \[\operatorname{lin}D=A^{-1}(\operatorname{lin}K).\] Moreover, \(D\) is pointed if and only if \(\ker A=\{0\}\) and \(K\cap A(V)\) is pointed in \(A(V)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lineality pulls back exactly. A pullback is pointed precisely when the map is injective and the target cone's range section is pointed.
knowledge_statements.title: Lineality and Pointedness of Pullback Cones

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint substitution for finitely represented cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(K=\{y\in W:By\geq0\}\), then \[A^{-1}(K)=\{x\in V:BAx\geq0\}.\] Consequently, finite-dimensional inverse images of polyhedral cones are polyhedral and closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pulling back an inequality-described cone composes its constraint map with the linear map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A^{-1}(K)=\{x:BAx\geq0\}\), hence the pullback is polyhedral and closed.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Inequality Representation Under Pullback

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relative Interior of a Qualified Pullback
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional inverse-image relative-interior rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(A(V)\cap\operatorname{ri}K\neq\varnothing\), then \[\operatorname{ri}(A^{-1}(K))=A^{-1}(\operatorname{ri}K).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the map range meets the target cone's relative interior, relative interior commutes with pullback.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq W\) is a nonempty convex cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Relative Interior of a Qualified Pullback

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X,Y\) be real vector spaces, let \(A:X\to Y\) be linear, and let \(Q\subseteq Y\) be a cone.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition is valid algebraically. Statements about closedness additionally assume topological vector spaces and continuity of \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The inverse-image, or pullback, cone of \(Q\) through \(A\) is \[A^{-1}Q:=\{x\in X:Ax\in Q\}.\] It is a cone because \(A(\lambda x)=\lambda Ax\). If \(Q\) is convex, then \(A^{-1}Q\) is convex. If \(X,Y\) are topological vector spaces, \(A\) is continuous, and \(Q\) is closed, then \(A^{-1}Q\) is closed. Its lineality contains \(\ker A\), and membership depends only on the coset \(x+\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inverse image of a cone \(Q\) under a linear map \(A\) consists of all domain vectors whose images lie in \(Q\). It is always a cone and inherits convexity from \(Q\). Under continuity, it also inherits closedness. Every vector in the kernel belongs to the pullback whenever \(0\in Q\), and adding a kernel vector does not change membership.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A^{-1}Q=\{x\in X:Ax\in Q\}\) is a cone; it is convex when \(Q\) is convex and closed when \(A\) is continuous and \(Q\) is closed.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(x\in A^{-1}Q\iff Ax\in Q\).
If \(\pi:X\to X/\ker A\), then \(A^{-1}Q=\pi^{-1}(\widetilde A^{-1}(Q\cap\operatorname{ran}A))\).
special_cases_latex: For a scalar functional \(a^*:X\to\mathbb R\), \((a^*)^{-1}(\mathbb R_+)\) is a homogeneous halfspace.
boundary_notes: Unlike forward images, continuous inverse images always preserve closedness.
Equality in the inverse-image rule for sums need not hold without additional range conditions.

notation.meaning: set-theoretic inverse image of Q under A

children.title: Quotient Cones
children.top_down_role: Conic structures obtained after collapsing linear subspaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual of a Quotient Cone
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the canonical identification of quotient functionals with functionals annihilating the collapsed subspace, the quotient cone's dual is the intersection of the original dual with that annihilator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space, let \(L\subseteq V\) be a linear subspace, and let \(q:V\to V/L\) be the quotient map. Identify \((V/L)^*\) with
\[
L^\circ=\{f\in V^*:f(\ell)=0\ \forall\ell\in L\}
\]
through \(q^*\). For every convex cone \(C\subseteq V\),
\[
q^*((q(C))^*)=C^*\cap L^\circ.
\]
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space.
\(q:V\to V/L\) is the canonical quotient map.
Dual cones use the nonnegative-pairing convention.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional quotient duality under the canonical identification of the quotient dual with the annihilator of the collapsed subspace.

knowledge_statements.title: Quotient Cones
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quotient cone comprises cosets represented by cone elements. Its lift is the cone enlarged by the collapsed subspace, whose closedness controls quotient closedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The cone induced by \(C\) in the quotient space is
\[
C/L:=q(C)=\{x+L:x\in C\}=(C+L)/L.
\]
It is a convex cone in \(V/L\). Its saturation in \(V\) is
\[
q^{-1}(C/L)=C+L.
\]
If \(V\) is finite-dimensional, then \(C/L\) is closed in \(V/L\) if and only if \(C+L\) is closed in \(V\). Thus quotienting can destroy closedness even when \(C\) is closed.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a real vector space and \(L\subseteq V\) is a linear subspace.
\(q:V\to V/L\) is the canonical quotient map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quotient cone is \(q(C)=(C+L)/L\), and its full lift is \(q^{-1}(q(C))=C+L\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cone induced after identifying vectors that differ by an element of a subspace.

notation.meaning: Canonical coset map onto the quotient space.
Cone induced in the quotient space.

6.1 Convex Cones p. 111

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact algebraic criterion for pointedness after collapsing a subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=q(C)\) and \(S=C+L=q^{-1}(D)\). Then \[q^{-1}(D\cap(-D))=S\cap(-S).\] Consequently, \[D\text{ is pointed}\iff (C+L)\cap(-(C+L))=L.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quotient cone is pointed exactly when the lineality of its saturated lift is the collapsed subspace.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a real vector space, \(L\subseteq V\) is a linear subspace, and \(q:V\to V/L\) is the quotient map.
knowledge_statements.title: Pointedness Criterion for Quotient Cones

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correspondence between quotient cones and cones invariant along quotient fibers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The assignments \(D\mapsto q^{-1}(D)\) and \(S\mapsto q(S)\) are mutually inverse, inclusion-preserving correspondences between convex cones \(D\subseteq V/L\) and convex cones \(S\subseteq V\) satisfying \(S+L=S\). In particular, \(q^{-1}(q(C))=C+L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cones in a quotient correspond exactly to cones upstairs that are saturated under addition of the collapsed subspace.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a real vector space, \(L\subseteq V\) is a linear subspace, and \(q:V\to V/L\) is canonical.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{D\subseteq V/L:D\text{ convex cone}\}\longleftrightarrow\{S\subseteq V:S\text{ convex cone and }S+L=S\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Saturated-Cone Correspondence

children.title: Closedness under Cone Operations
children.top_down_role: Closure-preserving regimes and failures for sums and linear images.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_m,Y\) be Hausdorff topological vector spaces, and let \(\mathcal O\) be a set operation defined on tuples of cones \((K_1,\ldots,K_m)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition separates the property of an operation on a specified class from the fact that a particular output happens to be closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a class \(\mathfrak C\) of closed cones, the operation \(\mathcal O\) is closedness preserving on \(\mathfrak C\) if \[(K_1,\ldots,K_m)\in\mathfrak C^m\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \mathcal O(K_1,\ldots,K_m)\text{ is closed}.\] Intersections and continuous linear inverse images are unconditionally closedness preserving. Minkowski sums and continuous linear forward images are only conditionally closedness preserving: their output may fail to be closed for closed unbounded convex cones. A closedness regime is a specified collection of hypotheses—such as polyhedrality, compactness, or a recession-nullspace condition—under which the implication holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cone operation is closedness preserving on a stated class when applying it to closed cones from that class always produces a closed set. Intersections and inverse images under continuous linear maps have this property without further regularity. Sums and forward linear images do not; for them, a closedness regime consists of additional hypotheses that guarantee the output is closed.
assumptions_latex: Every input cone \(K_i\) belongs to the declared class \(\mathfrak C\).
All topological and continuity conditions used by \(\mathcal O\) are included in the declared regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal O\) is closedness preserving on \(\mathfrak C\) exactly when closed inputs in \(\mathfrak C\) always yield a closed output.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\mathcal O(\mathfrak C^m)\subseteq\{C:C\text{ is closed}\}\).
A failure is witnessed by closed \(K_i\in\mathfrak C\) with \(\operatorname{cl}\mathcal O(K_1,\ldots,K_m)\neq\mathcal O(K_1,\ldots,K_m)\).
special_cases_latex: \(\mathcal O((K_i)_{i\in I})=\bigcap_{i\in I}K_i\) preserves closedness.
\(\mathcal O(K)=A^{-1}K\) preserves closedness when \(A\) is continuous.
immediate_consequences_latex: Polyhedral linear-image regimes are closedness preserving in finite dimensions.
A counterexample for projections is also a counterexample for general linear images.
boundary_notes: Convexity preservation and closedness preservation are distinct properties.
The closure \(\operatorname{cl}(K_1+K_2)\) is always closed, but inserting closure changes the original operation.

notation.meaning: declared class of admissible closed cones

children.title: Closedness of Cone Sums
children.top_down_role: Regular and irregular additive closure regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Sufficient Regimes for Closed Cone Sums
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sum of closed cones is closed when one summand is polyhedral or when the cones contain no nonzero mutually opposite directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K,L\subseteq V\) be closed convex cones in a finite-dimensional real vector space. The sum \(K+L\) is closed if either one summand is polyhedral or \(K\cap(-L)=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L\text{ polyhedral or }K\text{ polyhedral or }K\cap(-L)=\{0\}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad K+L\text{ is closed}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional closure guarantees for binary sums of closed convex cones.

notation.meaning: Directions in one cone whose negatives belong to the other cone.

knowledge_statements.title: Closedness of Cone Sums
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even two closed convex cones can have a nonclosed sum. Here a sequence in the sum converges to a matrix outside the sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Both \(K\) and \(L\) are closed convex cones, but \(K+L\) is not closed. In particular, the sequence
\[
Z_n=\begin{pmatrix}1/n&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\in K+L
\]
converges to
\[
Z=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\notin K+L.
\]
Thus closedness is not preserved by Minkowski addition of closed convex cones, even in finite dimensions.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb S^2\) is the space of real symmetric \(2\times2\) matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The closed convex cones \(K\) and \(L\) have a nonclosed Minkowski sum \(K+L\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit finite-dimensional pathology showing that closed cone sums need not be closed.

notation.meaning: One-dimensional linear subspace generated by the lower-right matrix unit.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional bipolar formula, retaining the closure required for nonclosed sums.

Dual cones use the nonnegative-pairing convention.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C,D\) be closed convex cones in a finite-dimensional real vector space. If either \(C\) or \(D\) is polyhedral, then \(C+D\) is closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding a polyhedral cone to a closed convex cone preserves closedness in finite dimensions.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space and let \(K_1,\ldots,K_m\subseteq X\) be nonempty closed convex cones.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition concerns ordinary Minkowski addition. The listed recession condition is a standard sufficient regime, not part of the bare definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Minkowski sum is \[K_1+\cdots+K_m:=\{x_1+\cdots+x_m:x_i\in K_i\}.\] The family has the closed-sum property when \(K_1+\cdots+K_m\) is closed in \(X\). Equivalently, whenever \(x^k=\sum_i x_i^k\) with \(x_i^k\in K_i\) and \(x^k\to x\), there exist \(x_i\in K_i\) such that \(x=\sum_i x_i\). For cones, the sufficient recession condition from the general closed-sum criterion becomes: \(d_i\in K_i\) and \(\sum_i d_i=0\) imply \(d_i\in K_i\cap(-K_i)\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sum of cones consists of all sums formed by choosing one vector from each cone. A family has the closed-sum property if every limit of such sums is itself representable as a sum of members of the cones. Closedness is not automatic. A standard sufficient condition excludes nonlineal recession directions from cancelling across the cones.
assumptions_latex: \(K_i\subseteq X\) is a nonempty closed convex cone for each \(i=1,\ldots,m\).
The topology on finite-dimensional \(X\) is its usual vector-space topology.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For every convergent sequence \(\sum_i x_i^k\to x\) with \(x_i^k\in K_i\), one has \(x\in\sum_iK_i\).
The addition map \(\Sigma:X^m\to X\), \(\Sigma(x_1,\ldots,x_m)=\sum_i x_i\), has closed image on \(K_1\times\cdots\times K_m\).
special_cases_latex: A finite sum of polyhedral cones is polyhedral and closed.
If every \(K_i\) is pointed and \(d_i\in K_i\), \(\sum_i d_i=0\) implies every \(d_i=0\), then the sufficient cancellation condition holds.
immediate_consequences_latex: For two cones, failure of closedness means \(\operatorname{cl}(K_1+K_2)\setminus(K_1+K_2)\neq\varnothing\).
Closed-sum criteria are instances of closedness criteria for linear images of product cones.
boundary_notes: Closedness of each summand alone is insufficient.
The algebraic sum remains a convex cone even when it is not closed.

notation.meaning: linear addition map on the product space

For closed convex cones \(K\) and \(L\),

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(K\) and \(L\) are closed convex cones in finite dimensions and at least one summand is polyhedral, then their Minkowski sum \(K+L\) is closed.

children.title: Closedness of Linear Images
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral, facial, and transversality criteria for image closedness.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Description of the Image Closure
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closure of a linear cone image is determined by dual vectors whose adjoint images lie in the cone dual; strict negative pairing certifies exclusion from that closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq X\) be a convex cone and \(A:X\to Y\) be linear between finite-dimensional inner-product spaces. Then \[(A(C))^*=\{z\in Y:A^*z\in C^*\}\] and \[\overline{A(C)}=\{y\in Y:\langle z,y\rangle\geq0\text{ whenever }A^*z\in C^*\}.\] Consequently, \(y\notin\overline{A(C)}\) exactly when some \(z\) satisfies \(A^*z\in C^*\) and \(\langle z,y\rangle<0\).
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq X\) is a convex cone and \(A:X\to Y\) is linear.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-dual convention; the formula characterizes the closure even when the image is nonclosed.

knowledge_statements.title: Lineality-Adjusted Transversality Criterion
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cone image is closed when the map's kernel meets the cone only along lineality directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq X\) be a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional space, let \(L=C\cap(-C)\), and let \(A:X\to Y\) be linear. If \[C\cap\ker A=L,\] then \(A(C)\) is closed.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq X\) is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extension of the trivial-kernel criterion allowing kernel directions already contained in the cone's lineality.

knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Interior Kernel Criterion
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the kernel meets the relative interior of a cone, the cone image equals the image of its span and is closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a nonempty convex cone in a finite-dimensional real vector space and let \(A\) be linear. If \[\ker A\cap\operatorname{ri}C\ne\varnothing,\] then \[A(C)=A(\operatorname{span}C).\] Consequently, \(A(C)\) is a linear subspace and is closed.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a nonempty convex cone in a finite-dimensional real vector space.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A transversality regime in which the cone image becomes a linear subspace.

notation.meaning: Relative interior of C in its span

knowledge_statements.title: Kernel-Saturation Criterion for Image Closedness
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear cone image is closed exactly when the cone saturated by the map's kernel is closed, equivalently when its quotient image is closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq X\) be a convex cone and \(A:X\to Y\) be linear between finite-dimensional spaces. Then \[A^{-1}(A(C))=C+\ker A,\] and \[A(C)\text{ is closed in }Y\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad C+\ker A\text{ is closed in }X.\] Equivalently, the image of \(C\) in \(X/\ker A\) is closed.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq X\) is a convex cone and \(A:X\to Y\) is linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A(C)\text{ is closed}\iff C+\ker A\text{ is closed}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-dimensional reduction to the quotient by the kernel.

knowledge_statements.title: Closedness of Linear Images
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear image of a closed cone is closed when the cone is polyhedral or meets the map's kernel only at zero; closedness can otherwise fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq X\) be a closed convex cone and let \(A:X\to Y\) be linear. If \(C\) is polyhedral, then \(A(C)\) is a polyhedral cone and hence is closed. Independently, if the transversality condition \(C\cap\ker A=\{0\}\) holds, then \(A(C)\) is closed. Thus polyhedrality and trivial intersection with the kernel are two sufficient mechanisms for closedness; absent such a condition, linear images of closed convex cones need not be closed.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
\(C\subseteq X\) is a closed convex cone and \(A:X\to Y\) is linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A(C)\) is closed if \(C\) is polyhedral or if \(C\cap\ker A=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional sufficient criteria; no claim that every closed-cone image is closed.

notation.meaning: Image of the cone under the linear map

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X,Y\) be finite-dimensional real vector spaces, let \(K\subseteq X\) be a nonempty closed convex cone, and let \(A:X\to Y\) be linear.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition is finite-dimensional. It records common sufficient regimes but does not identify them as necessary in full generality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The pair \((K,A)\) has the closed-image property when \[AK=\{Ax:x\in K\}=\operatorname{cl}(AK).\] Equivalently, every convergent sequence \(Ax_k\to y\) with \(x_k\in K\) has some \(x\in K\) satisfying \(Ax=y\). Since the recession cone of a closed convex cone is \(K\) and its lineality space is \(\operatorname{lin}K:=K\cap(-K)\), a standard sufficient condition is \[K\cap\ker A\subseteq\operatorname{lin}K.\] Polyhedral cones also have closed images under every linear map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed convex cone and a linear map have the closed-image property if the image cone contains all its limit points. Sequentially, every limit of vectors \(Ax_k\), with \(x_k\in K\), must equal \(Ax\) for some \(x\in K\). A standard sufficient condition says that every cone direction annihilated by \(A\) must be a lineality direction. Polyhedral cones satisfy the property for all linear maps.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq X\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The closed-image property is \(AK=\operatorname{cl}(AK)\); it holds in particular if \(K\cap\ker A\subseteq K\cap(-K)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(y_k=Ax_k\to y,\ x_k\in K\Rightarrow y\in AK\).
The restricted mapping \(A|_K:K\to Y\) is a closed-set-valued image at the level of its total range.
special_cases_latex: If \(K\cap\ker A=\{0\}\), then the recession-nullspace sufficient condition holds.
If \(K\) is polyhedral, then \(AK\) is polyhedral and closed.
immediate_consequences_latex: Closedness of \(AK\) guarantees that conic feasibility limits in the image space remain feasible.
Closedness of cone sums follows by applying this property to the addition map on a product cone.
boundary_notes: Injectivity is sufficient but not necessary.
Closedness of \(K\) and continuity of \(A\) alone do not imply closedness of \(AK\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq X\) be a convex cone and let \(A:X\to Y\) be linear, where \(X,Y\) are finite-dimensional. knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let K_1,\ldots,K_m\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n be nonempty convex cones. Suppose that z_i\in\operatorname{cl}K_i for i=1,\ldots,m and \sum_{i=1}^m z_i=0 imply z_i\in\operatorname{lin}(\operatorname{cl}K_i) for every i. Then \operatorname{cl}\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^mK_i\right)=\sum_{i=1}^m\operatorname{cl}K_i.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonclosed Projection Pathologies
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projecting a two-by-two positive semidefinite matrix to its first diagonal and off-diagonal entries yields a nonclosed set: it contains every pair with positive first coordinate and the origin, but excludes every other pair whose first coordinate is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(P:\mathbb S^2\to\mathbb R^2\) by \(P\!\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&b\\b&c\end{smallmatrix}\right)=(a,b)\). Then \[P(\mathbb S_+^2)=\{(a,b)\in\mathbb R^2:a>0\}\cup\{(0,0)\}.\] This image is not closed: the sequence \((1/n,1)\) lies in it and converges to \((0,1)\), which does not lie in it.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb S^2\) carries its usual Euclidean topology.
\(\mathbb S_+^2\) is the cone of positive semidefinite real symmetric \(2\times2\) matrices.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X=U\oplus V\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space, let \(P_U:X\to U\) be the canonical projection, and let \(K\subseteq X\) be a closed convex cone or closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition applies to cones and more general closed convex sets. The blueprint's conic case is obtained by requiring \(K\) to be a cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonclosed projection pathology occurs when \[P_UK\neq\operatorname{cl}(P_UK).\] Equivalently, there exist \(u_k\in P_UK\) and \(\bar u\in U\) such that \(u_k\to\bar u\) but \(\bar u\notin P_UK\). Choosing lifts \(u_k+v_k\in K\), the pathology means that projected coordinates converge while no lift \(\bar u+v\in K\) exists. For a cone, the missing-limit set \(\operatorname{cl}(P_UK)\setminus P_UK\) is conic under positive scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projection pathology is the failure of a projected closed convex set or cone to remain closed. It is witnessed by projected points converging to a limit that has no feasible lift in the original set. The eliminated coordinates of chosen lifts may escape without producing a limit in the original space. In the conic case, positive multiples of a missing projected limit are again missing unless they collapse to the origin.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq U\oplus V\) is closed and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pathology is \(\operatorname{cl}(P_UK)\setminus P_UK\neq\varnothing\), equivalently the existence of a convergent projected sequence with an unattainable limit.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \((\exists\bar u\in U)\ [\bar u\in\operatorname{cl}(P_UK)\ \wedge\ K\cap(\bar u+V)=\varnothing]\).
The set-valued fiber map \(u\mapsto K\cap(u+V)\) has nonempty fibers along a sequence approaching a point with empty fiber.
special_cases_latex: The projection of \(\{(x_1,x_2):x_1>0,x_2>0,x_1x_2\geq1\}\) onto the first coordinate is the nonclosed ray \((0,\infty)\).
A nonclosed sum pathology is a projection pathology for the addition map on a Cartesian product.
immediate_consequences_latex: A nonclosed projection is a nonclosed linear image.
Replacing \(P_UK\) by its closure adds limit-feasible points not represented by exact lifts.
boundary_notes: The cited explicit example is a closed convex set rather than a cone; conic nonclosed images require nonpolyhedral cone constructions.
Metric projection onto a closed convex set is unrelated to this coordinate-projection pathology.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polar and Dual Cones in a Hilbert Space
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal H\) be a real Hilbert space with inner product \(\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle\), and let \(C\subseteq\mathcal H\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This record uses the nonpositive polar convention. The positive dual cone is its negative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The polar cone and dual cone of \(C\) are \[C^{\ominus}:=\{u\in\mathcal H:(\forall x\in C)\ \langle x,u\rangle\leq0\},\qquad C^{\oplus}:=-C^{\ominus}=\{u:(\forall x\in C)\ \langle x,u\rangle\geq0\}.\] Both are nonempty closed convex cones and depend only on the closed convex conical hull of \(C\). Polarity reverses inclusion. The bipolar \(C^{\ominus\ominus}\) recovers the closed convex conical hull of \(C\), so polarity converts primal conic geometry into inequalities in the paired space and back.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The polar cone contains all vectors having nonpositive inner product with every point of \(C\). The dual cone uses the opposite, nonnegative sign and equals the negative of the polar. These cones are always closed and convex, reverse inclusions, and ignore any difference between \(C\) and its closed convex conical hull. Applying the nonpositive polar twice returns that hull.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) is a real Hilbert space.
\(C\subseteq\mathcal H\) is arbitrary for polarity; bipolar recovery assumes \(C\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C^{\ominus}=\{u:\sup_{x\in C}\langle x,u\rangle\leq0\}\), \(C^{\oplus}=-C^{\ominus}\), and \(C^{\ominus\ominus}=\overline{\operatorname{cone}}C\) for nonempty convex \(C\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(u\in C^{\ominus}\iff\sigma_C(u)\leq0\), where \(\sigma_C(u)=\sup_{x\in C}\langle x,u\rangle\).
\(C^{\ominus}=(\overline{\operatorname{cone}}\operatorname{conv}C)^{\ominus}\).
special_cases_latex: If \(L\) is a linear subspace, then \(L^{\ominus}=L^{\oplus}=L^{\perp}\).
A closed convex cone \(K\) is self-dual when \(K=K^{\oplus}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: \(D\subseteq C\Rightarrow C^{\ominus}\subseteq D^{\ominus}\).
\((K_1+K_2)^{\ominus}=K_1^{\ominus}\cap K_2^{\ominus}\) for nonempty cones.
boundary_notes: Some literature writes the nonnegative dual as \(K^*\) and calls it the polar.
For general dual-paired spaces, the polar lies in the paired dual space rather than in the primal space.
